chapter: Europe tours, Birdland memories and closing
title: Ben Barth made Dinah a star; the Keynote session at the Apollo
summary: Cobb says Ben Barth built Dinah's career, and recalls a Keynote session at the Apollo with Buckner that ran until 5 a.m., and his own hustle selling Swing Books.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: But she, of course, at this time wasn't quite the big star she was going to become.
No, she got to be the star because Big Ben Barth Barr made her.
Oh, sure. Sure. He put -- now, we did a thing. We were in the Apollo Theater for -- what the hell's the name of this record company that -- Linn --
We did a session working in the Apollo Theater -- (inaudible) in the morning. And that's when

"Dinah did, I Know How To Do It," Salty Papa Blues." Remember this? She did four sides that morning. Milton Buckner was on that set. Even Hamp played two finger pianos on it, but he -- she couldn't record with him. Well, Hamp wanted to get in on the deal.

I made that next -- first show the next morning with one eye open, because we had to take some liquor on that date to keep our eyes open and keep happy. We recorded until 5:00 in the morning. And our (inaudible) hour was 10:30. Listen to me.

We were (inaudible) show people were standing three abreast from 7th Avenue all the way over to 8th Avenue, both sides of that theater with that band. That was the damndest band, and they did it in Philadelphia. I could name anyplace that -- in the rain with umbrellas, waiting to get in, and I'm selling the Lionel Hampton Swing Book got my wife out in the lobby, and I'm making a quarter out of every book. Shoot, I was cleaning up too.
I've been hustling all my life, you know. I had to hustle to (Inaudible) would
make me a quarter. Well, you need money to live on, because I just told you I don't want a lot. I just want to be comfortable. That's all.
